name: sdk-mcp-tool-call
note: Every line that crossed the real claude.exe's stdin (to-program) and stdout (from-program) while Tarsee's engine ran one turn through the Agent SDK 0.3.319. t is milliseconds from the start of the turn.

tools.name: tarsee_send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a channel (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Slack, email, or web chat). Use this to proactively notify the user. For email, channel_id MUST be the target address; for threaded email replies with In-Reply-To headers, use tarsee_send_email_thread instead.

channel_id.description: Specific chat/channel ID (auto-resolved if omitted — required for email)

tools.name: tarsee_send_file
tools.description: Send a file as a real attachment (PDF, HTML report, image, audio, video, zip, spreadsheet, anything) to a Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp or Slack chat, or to one of the dashboard's own chats (web: a card there that opens in the viewer). Use it whenever someone asks for a file or you made one for them: never answer with a folder path or a download link instead, and never say a channel can't take attachments. With no channel_id it goes to the chat you are talking in (on Slack, the same thread; else that channel's most recent chat). The file must already exist; a relative path is read from the workspace. Size caps: Telegram 50 MB, Discord 25 MB, WhatsApp 16 MB, Slack 100 MB, web 50 MB. For email, use tarsee_send_email_thread with attachments.

channel.description: Channel to send to: the one you are talking in, unless asked otherwise (web: one of the dashboard's own chats; channel_id is its conversation id, the one you are in by default)

file_path.description: Absolute path, or a path relative to the workspace

caption.description: Optional words sent with the file (Telegram shows up to 1024 characters)

channel_id.description: Specific chat/channel ID; leave it out to send to the chat you are in

tools.name: tarsee_configure_email_channel
tools.description: Configure the email channel when the user tells you their IMAP/SMTP credentials in chat. Partial-update — only the fields you pass get written; existing values stay. Passwords are stored encrypted. Call this instead of asking the user to open Settings. Infer common provider hosts (Gmail: imap.gmail.com:993 / smtp.gmail.com:465; iCloud: imap.mail.me.com:993 / smtp.mail.me.com:587; Zoho: imap.zoho.com:993 / smtp.zoho.com:465; FastMail: imap.fastmail.com:993 / smtp.fastmail.com:465) from the user's email domain when they don't specify. Outlook.com, Hotmail and Microsoft 365 mailboxes cannot connect this way: Microsoft refuses app passwords for IMAP and requires its own sign-in, so tell the user to use a mailbox from another provider instead of saving one.

tarseeEmailAddress.description: The mailbox Tarsee answers at, e.g. 'tarsee@yourcompany.com'

user.description: Usually the same as the mailbox address

allowlistFromAddresses.description: Only reply to emails from these addresses. Empty = accept from anyone (dev mode — warn the user).

mentionKeyword.description: Without leading @. Default 'tarsee'. Tarsee only replies when the body contains this mention.

replyAllMarker.description: Subject marker that opts into reply-all. Default '[reply-all]'.

fromName.description: Display name on outbound mail. Default 'Tarsee'.

enabled.description: Toggle the channel on/off. Leave undefined to preserve current state.

tools.name: tarsee_send_email_thread
tools.description: Start a new email thread or reply to an existing one with proper threading headers (In-Reply-To + References). Use this for proactive outbound email — you don't need to wait for the recipient to email first. Body is plain text; no markdown formatting survives email well. For replies, pass inReplyTo with the Message-ID from the inbound email. Attach files with attachments (paths on disk).

to.description: Primary recipient(s). Single address string or array.

subject.description: Subject line (Tarsee adds 'Re: ' automatically when inReplyTo is set)

inReplyTo.description: Message-ID of the email you're replying to (include angle brackets). Omit for new threads.

attachments.description: Files to attach as real attachments: absolute paths, or paths relative to the workspace. Never paste a file's contents or a folder path into the body instead.

tools.name: tarsee_schedule_task
tools.description:
Schedule a task using cron syntax. Supports one-time and recurring. For simple notifications, use action (direct, instant). For complex tasks, use prompt (AI session).

Only schedule a task when the owner asks for one, or has said yes when you offered: every run of a prompt task is a paid turn on the AI. A task you schedule starts paused, and won't run until the owner switches it on, in Settings > Automation > Scheduled tasks or by sending /cron on <id>. Say so when you save one, with its id. You can't schedule tasks while running a scheduled task, the heartbeat or BOOT.md.

EXAMPLES:
- One-time reminder: schedule='30 12 7 4 *', once=true, action={tool:'send_message', args:{channel:'telegram', message:'Meeting now!'}}
- Daily recurring: schedule='0 8 * * *', action={tool:'send_message', args:{channel:'telegram', message:'Good morning!'}}
- Complex: schedule='0 8 * * 1', prompt='Check calendar and summarize the week'

ALWAYS prefer action over prompt for send_message tasks. Set once=true for one-time reminders (auto-deletes after firing). A prompt task runs at most once every 15 minutes (5-part schedules, no seconds). Cron expressions are interpreted in UTC — call tarsee_datetime to confirm the current local time before scheduling.

schedule.description: Cron expression. Format: 'min hour day month weekday'. Interpreted in UTC.

once.description: If true, job auto-deletes after firing once. Use for one-time reminders.

prompt.description: AI prompt for complex tasks (each run is a full, paid AI session)

action.description: Direct tool action — instant, no AI needed. Use for simple notifications.

tools.name: tarsee_remember
tools.description: Save an important fact or note to long-term memory. This persists across conversations and restarts.

content.description: The fact or note to remember

tools.name: tarsee_daily_log
tools.description: Append an entry to today's daily memory log (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md).

tools.name: tarsee_read_file
tools.description: Read a Tarsee workspace file (SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md, etc.) or a daily memory log.

tools.name: tarsee_write_file
tools.description: Write or overwrite a Tarsee workspace file. Use for updating personality, identity, memory, or user notes. HEARTBEAT.md (the heartbeat's checks) and BOOT.md (what runs when Tarsee restarts) can be written too, but what you write there doesn't run until the owner OKs it in Settings > Automation (Let it run; for BOOT.md, Run at each restart): tell the owner so, and never say it is set up or running before then. The same goes for a change made with your own file or shell tools.

tools.name: tarsee_search_memories
tools.description: Search through all memory files for a keyword or phrase.

tools.name: tarsee_search_memories_deep
tools.description: Deep semantic search — reads ALL memories, MEMORY.md, and last 30 daily logs so you can reason about what's relevant. Use when keyword search returns nothing or the query is vague/conceptual.

query.description: What you're looking for — natural language description

tools.name: tarsee_create_canvas
tools.description: Create an interactive HTML/CSS/JS canvas — renders as a live iframe in chat. Use for dashboards, charts, visualizations, mini-apps, calculators, or any interactive UI the user requests.

title.description: Canvas title/ID (used in URL, lowercase, hyphens ok)

html.description: HTML content (the body, no need for full document)

tools.name: tarsee_create_diagram
tools.description: Render a clickable flowchart/diagram in chat. Use for multi-step processes, workflows, architecture, decision trees. Each clickable node triggers a follow-up question when the user clicks it.

tools.name: tarsee_datetime
tools.description: Get current date/time/day or convert timezones. ALWAYS use this for dates and days of the week — never guess.

date.description: Date to check, e.g. '2026-04-17' or 'next friday'

tools.name: tarsee_calculator
tools.description: Evaluate a math expression with precision. Use for ANY math — arithmetic, percentages, conversions, financial calculations. Never do math in your head.

tools.name: tarsee_discord_admin
tools.description:
Admin jobs in a Discord server the bot is in, done by Tarsee's own logged-in bot: list_channels, create_channel (text, voice or category; public, private for listed people and roles, or with another channel's access), edit_channel (name, topic, category, who can see or do what), create_webhook, list_webhooks. Use it whenever someone asks for a new channel, a private channel, a webhook or a permission change. It replaces any Discord REST call from Bash: never pull DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN from the vault for this, and never put a bot token or a webhook URL in a command.

GET THE GO FIRST for anything that changes a server, following the approval rules in your instructions (AGENTS.md). A new webhook counts as a credential (its URL lets anyone post), so create_webhook needs the owner's go. Put who said go, in their words, in approved_by (it is logged and shows in the server's audit log). If nobody has said go for this exact change, ask instead. list_channels and list_webhooks need no go.

THE SERVER: guild_id, or channel_id of any channel in it (the one you are answering in works), or nothing when the bot is in one server only.

WEBHOOK URLS ARE SECRETS: create_webhook saves the URL in the vault under save_as_key (e.g. ALERTS_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK; say what it is for in purpose) and returns only the webhook id, the key name and a masked URL. Scripts and services read it from the vault by that key name. reveal: true puts the full URL in the result: only when the owner asks to see it themselves, never for anything that goes into a chat.

NOTHING HERE DELETES: deleting a channel or a webhook is for the owner to do by hand; say so if asked. If Discord refuses for a missing permission, the error says which one and where: tell the person, do not try another way around it.

guild_id.description: The server's id. Optional: channel_id of any channel in it works too, and with one server neither is needed

channel_id.description: edit_channel, create_webhook, list_webhooks: the channel to act on. list_channels, create_channel: any channel in the server (e.g. the one you are answering in), only to find the server

approved_by.description: Required for create_channel, edit_channel and create_webhook: who said go and for what, e.g. "the owner in #general: make #alerts and a webhook for the watchdog"

name.description: create_channel: the new channel's name. edit_channel: its new name. create_webhook: the webhook's name, shown on its posts

type.description: create_channel: the kind of channel (default text)

parent_id.description: create_channel: the category to put it in. edit_channel: the category to move it to, or "none" to take it out of its category

topic.description: Text channels: the topic line (an empty string clears it in edit_channel)

near_channel_id.description: create_channel: put the new channel next to this one (it goes in the same category unless parent_id says otherwise)

place.description: create_channel with near_channel_id: before or after it (default after)

private.description: create_channel, edit_channel: true hides it from @everyone and lets in only the bot, allow_user_ids and allow_role_ids (and server admins). edit_channel false: @everyone's view goes back to the default

allow_user_ids.description: With private: true, the Discord user ids who may see and use it

allow_role_ids.description: With private: true, the role ids whose members may see and use it

copy_permissions_from.description: create_channel: give the new channel the same access as this channel (instead of private). Without either, a channel in a category gets the category's access, and one outside any category is public

sync_with_category.description: edit_channel: replace its access with its category's (the new one when parent_id is given)

permissions.description: edit_channel: who may see or do what in the channel

target.description: A user id, a role id, or "everyone"

target_type.description: Only if the id could be either

allow.description: Permissions to allow, e.g. ViewChannel, SendMessages, ReadMessageHistory, Connect, Speak (or view, send, history)

reset.description: Permissions to set back to the default (neither allowed nor denied here)

clear.description: true removes this target's whole overwrite on the channel

save_as_key.description: create_webhook: the vault key name for the URL, capitals and underscores, e.g. ALERTS_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK (default DISCORD_WEBHOOK_<CHANNEL>). An existing key is never replaced unless overwrite_key is true

purpose.description: create_webhook: what the webhook is for, saved with the vault key, e.g. "uptime watchdog alerts"

overwrite_key.description: create_webhook: replace a vault key of that name that is already there

use_bot_avatar.description: create_webhook: give the webhook the bot's own picture

reveal.description: create_webhook: also return the full URL. Only when the owner asks to see it themselves; never for anything that goes into a chat

tools.name: tarsee_railway
tools.description:
Railway jobs done by Tarsee itself with a Railway token it reads from the vault (RAILWAY_API_TOKEN): list_projects (projects; with project, its environments and services), list_variables (variable NAMES on a service, never values), set_variable (set one variable on a service, then Railway redeploys it as it does on any variable change), redeploy (redeploy a service's latest deployment). Use it whenever someone asks to set a Railway variable or redeploy. It replaces any Railway call from Bash: never put a Railway token or a secret value in a command (no `railway variables --set` with a secret, no GraphQL with a token).

SECRETS GO THROUGH from_key: for anything secret (a token, a password, a webhook URL, a database URL) pass from_key, the vault key name that holds it (e.g. from_key: "ALERTS_WEBHOOK"). Tarsee reads the value itself; it never shows up in the result, the logs or your context, only a masked form. value is for plain, non-secret text only (a port, a flag, a public URL); a value that looks like a secret or is a vault key's value is refused.

GET THE GO FIRST for set_variable and redeploy: from the owner, or from whoever your instructions (AGENTS.md, USER.md) say may give it. Putting a secret into a service (from_key) counts as handing out a credential, so it needs the owner's go. Put who said go, in their words, in approved_by (it is logged). If nobody has said go for this exact change, ask instead. list_projects and list_variables need no go.

TARSEE'S OWN SERVICE: when Tarsee runs on Railway, leaving out project works on the project Tarsee runs in, in its environment, on its own service. Redeploying it, or setting a variable on it with a deploy, restarts Tarsee and ends the turn doing it: say so before you do it, and finish anything else first.

NAMES OR IDS: project, environment (default: the one Tarsee runs in, else production) and service each take a name (any case) or an id. A name that matches nothing, or more than one, is refused with the choices listed.

NOTHING HERE DELETES: deleting a variable, a service or a project is for the owner to do by hand in Railway; say so if asked. If Railway refuses, the error says why in plain words: tell the person, do not try another way around it.

project.description: The project's name (any case) or id. Leave it out for the project Tarsee runs in (on Railway); list_projects without it lists them all

environment.description: The environment's name or id (default: the one Tarsee runs in, else production)

service.description: list_variables, set_variable, redeploy: the service's name or id (default in Tarsee's own project: Tarsee's own service)

name.description: set_variable: the variable's name, e.g. ALERTS_WEBHOOK_URL

from_key.description: set_variable: the vault key whose value to set, for anything secret. The value is read by Tarsee and never shown

value.description: set_variable: a plain, NON-SECRET value. Anything secret goes in the vault and through from_key instead. Pass from_key or value, not both

deploy.description: set_variable: true (default) lets Railway redeploy the service as it normally does on a variable change; false sets it without a deploy (it takes effect on the next one)

approved_by.description: Required for set_variable and redeploy: who said go and for what, e.g. "the owner in chat: put the alerts webhook on the worker service"

tools.name: tarsee_browser
tools.description: Control a stealth web browser with captcha solving. Navigate pages, fill forms, click buttons, take screenshots, and auto-solve reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha/Turnstile. Browser persists across calls.

tools.name: tarsee_web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a URL and return its content (HTML converted to text, or raw for APIs).

tools.name: tarsee_web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return results.

tools.name: tarsee_pdf_read
tools.description: Read the text of a PDF: a file in the workspace (files people send in are saved in its uploads folder) or a web address. Long PDFs come a few pages at a time; the answer says which pages to ask for next. Use it whenever you need what a PDF says and can't open the file yourself. Scanned pages (pictures of text) have no text to read.

path.description: The PDF: a path in the workspace (absolute, or relative to it, e.g. 'uploads/report.pdf') or an http(s) address

pages.description: Which pages: '3', '2-5', or '6-' for page 6 to the end. Default: from page 1, as many as fit

max_chars.description: The most characters to return (default 10000, up to 50000)

tools.name: tarsee_get_key
tools.description: Get a value from the encrypted key vault. The session system prompt already includes an inventory of what's available — use this tool to fetch the actual value when you need to USE a key, not to check whether one exists.

key.description: Key name (matches an entry from the inventory)

tools.name: tarsee_set_key
tools.description: Store a value in the encrypted key vault. Use when the user gives you a new credential (API key, token, password) to remember across sessions.

key.description: Key name (uppercase with underscores, e.g. STRIPE_SECRET)

value.description: Secret value — stored encrypted at rest

description.description: What this key is for (surfaced in the next session's inventory)

tools.name: tarsee_list_keys
tools.description: Re-query the vault live for the current list of keys. The session system prompt already snapshots this at start, so only call this if you just set/deleted a key or suspect the inventory is stale. Returns names + descriptions only — values require tarsee_get_key.

tools.name: tarsee_delete_key
tools.description: Remove a key from the encrypted vault. Use when the user explicitly asks to forget or rotate a credential.

tools.name: tarsee_list_files
tools.description: List all Tarsee workspace files and their sizes.

tools.name: tarsee_push_notification
tools.description: Send a Web Push notification to all the user's registered devices (iPhone/iPad PWA, laptop browsers). Use this for time-sensitive pings — cron completions, webhook alerts, proactive reminders — when the user may not have the app open. Non-urgent follow-ups should use tarsee_send_message instead.

title.description: Short headline — appears as the notification title. Keep under 50 chars.

body.description: One- or two-sentence body. Keep under 200 chars; platforms truncate.

url.description: Deep-link URL on tap. Defaults to the app root. Use e.g. '/?conv=xxx' to jump to a specific conversation.

tag.description: Grouping tag — pushes with the same tag replace each other in the tray instead of stacking.
